newsitem.title: USA: U.S. S&P 500 futures close sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. S&P 500 futures close sharply higher.

text.p: U.S. Standard & Poor's 500 futures closed near the daily highs, reversing the trend in the first half of the day as technology stocks recouped losses, traders and analysts said.
March S&Ps rose to 815.50, near the short-term target of 815.00 that traders were calling for before the opening.

However, the outlook for a rise to 815.00 was dashed in early trade when one firm downgraded Cisco Systems Inc to neutral from buy and weakened the Nasdaq composite. The decline in the Nasdaq immediately pressured most stock index futures, they said.
March S&Ps fell to 804.10, below support at 806.00, but managed to find good intraday support around 808.00 to 808.40.
Overall positive short-term factors were highlighted once the Nasdaq composite loosened its grip on declines, they said.
Several traders noted heavy buy-stop orders at the 811.00 to 812.00 area. One trader earlier noted that 812.00 represented a trendline level on the hourly charts.
"Mondays are usually the best days of the week," one analyst said.
Monday's sharp reversal set the stage for a retest of the all-time high of 820.40 by mid-week, another analyst said.
The strong tone in most U.S. stock index futures spilled into the Nikkei futures pit, where June extended gains and closed near the daily high of 18,180.0.
Fair value for March S&Ps was at about 1.00 points to cash, with arbitrage buy programs at a premium of 2.20 points and arbitrage sell programs at a 0.30 point premium to cash.

At the end of pit trade, March S&Ps were up 7.80 at 815.00, the 2-1/2-week high, KCBT Value Lines were up 6.10 at 726.20, NYSE composites were up 4.05 at 428.65, Midcap 400s were up 1.30 at 268.85, Nasdaq 100s were 14.25 higher at 858.75, Russell 2000s were up 1.95 at 367.45, and June Nikkeis were up 135 at 18,170.
